scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a routine config change on CSW1, R1 lost an OSPF neighbor.
Internet traffic still works but uses only the CSW2 path. CSW1's
eth0 link to R1 is physically UP, IP addresses match, ping
between CSW1's eth0 (10.0.0.34) and R1's eth0 (10.0.0.33) works.
Why is no OSPF adjacency forming?

injection.action: mark the R1-facing interface as OSPF passive

pre_check.command: vtysh -c "show ip ospf interface eth0" | grep -i passive

post_inject_check.command: vtysh -c "show ip ospf interface eth0" | grep -i passive

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: csw1 OSPF passive-interface config on eth0
Mechanism: `passive-interface` tells OSPF to advertise the
  subnet but NOT to send hellos on it. The L2/L3 link is fine,
  but no OSPF adjacency forms because both ends never exchange
  hellos. r1 doesn't learn about networks reachable via csw1's
  eth0, and csw1 doesn't learn r1's loopback over this path.
Localization: csw1
Root cause: `passive-interface eth0` set on csw1's OSPF
  process when it should be active (eth0 faces a peer router)
Fix: `vtysh -c "router ospf" -c "no passive-interface eth0"`
  on csw1

injection.output:
This command is deprecated, because it is not VRF-aware.
Please, use "ip ospf passive" on an interface instead.

line.command: vtysh -c "show ip ospf interface eth0" | grep -i passive

agent.diagnosis_text:
The OSPF adjacency between CSW1 and R1 is broken because CSW1's eth0 interface
(10.0.0.34/30, the WAN link on segment CD_WAN_LINK_1) was marked as a passive
OSPF interface during the recent config change. The FRR running config on CSW1
contains an explicit `ip ospf passive` statement under `interface eth0`, confirmed
by `show ip ospf interface eth0` which reports "No Hellos (Passive interface)"
and zero neighbors on that interface.

A passive OSPF interface participates in the OSPF topology in one direction only:
the subnet is still advertised in LSAs (10.0.0.32/30 is present in CSW1's
`network` statement), so routing entries exist and ping works across the link.
However, the interface completely suppresses sending and processing OSPF Hello
packets. Without Hellos, R1's OSPF process (router-id 10.0.0.76) receives no
Hello from CSW1 and the adjacency never progresses beyond Init. This explains
exactly why the link is physically up, IPs are correct, ping succeeds, yet no
OSPF neighborship forms. R1 correctly has `network 10.0.0.32/30 area 0` and its
eth0 is not passive, so the fault is entirely on CSW1.

Root cause: `ip ospf passive` was incorrectly applied to CSW1's eth0 as part of
the routine config change, suppressing all OSPF Hello traffic on the CSW1–R1
link.

Corrective fix: Log into CSW1 and remove the passive flag:
  `conf t → interface eth0 → no ip ospf passive`
The adjacency will re-form within one Hello interval (10 s) and traffic will
resume dual-path load-sharing through both CSW1 and CSW2.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names CSW1 as the affected device and attributes the passive OSPF eth0 configuration to CSW1.
The agent explicitly identifies CSW1 eth0 as configured as a passive OSPF interface (ip ospf passive / passive-interface), matching the expected component.
The agent explicitly states the link is physically up and pings succeed (no L2/L3 failure), distinguishing the passive-interface problem from a link-down condition.
Removing the passive setting on CSW1's eth0 (no ip ospf passive) accomplishes the same remediation as the expected no passive-interface eth0 and will restore the OSPF adjacency.

The investigation log shows commands and outputs that directly identify CSW1's eth0 as OSPF-passive with no neighbors and that R1 lacks an adjacency; the agent's inference that passive-interface prevents Hellos and thus adjacency is sound. Some non-essential claims (LSA/advertise and ping) are asserted without explicit log evidence.
